ai_summary: Scotland continues to demonstrate near-total decarbonisation, operating at a clean carbon intensity of just 1 gCO2/kWh compared to 149 gCO2/kWh across Great Britain as a whole. Scottish wind output is currently delivering an estimated 3.7 GW, which represents 36.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity and accounts for over half of total GB wind output of 6.7 GW. However, severe cross-border transmission bottlenecks prevent this abundance of renewable electricity from reaching downstream demand centres. Consequently, 19.8 GWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, running up a constraint cost of about £658,390. To substitute for this blocked renewable generation, fossil generators fired up elsewhere on the network, burning an estimated 3,768,061 m3 of gas and releasing an additional 6,941 tonnes of CO2. Annualised at this daily pace, the total yearly cost of curtailment approaches approximately £240 million, ultimately increasing electricity invoices across the UK by an estimated £1/MWh through balancing charges. Eliminating these transmission limits remains essential to stopping this dual financial and environmental penalty.
